summary: Considering the growing number of virtual game users over the past decade, this project proposes the development of a game designed for children's aerospace education and training. The project was developed within the context of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer”. The player's objective is to complete missions involving survival, data collection, scientific research, data management, spacecraft and aircraft systems, and geological exploration. Throughout the narrative, scientific and technological topics are introduced, enabling players to learn different techniques and concepts while developing a basic understanding of aerospace engineering and natural sciences. Furthermore, in each mission, children perform activities to keep the space station operational, such as generating electricity using solar panels, monitoring crew health, investigating soil composition, treating water, and experimenting with different cultivation methods. The game was developed using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, as well as software development languages and technologies. Its design was inspired by the visual style of the game Stardew Valley, recreating regions of the planet Mars, specifically the Arcadia Planitia region. Interaction with the game encourages scientific, critical, and technological thinking, inspiring new generations of astronauts and scientists.

MARS ADVENTURES: EDUCATIONAL SIMULATOR FOR SCIENTIFIC PRACTICES AND SPACE SURVIVAL

This project aims to develop Mars Adventure, an educational digital game that combines adventure, survival and science, challenging players to remain on Mars by completing missions inspired by astronauts' activities and the obstacles involved in space exploration. Throughout the experience, activities will be developed related to the installation of solar panels, monitoring the astronaut's health, geological investigation, water identification and treatment, growing food in greenhouses, and protection against Martian environmental phenomena.

As a learning aid, the game features Capi, a capybara who acts as a tutor and virtual assistant, guiding the player through missions, explaining scientific concepts, and helping interpret the information presented. The choice of the capybara is related to its popularity and recognition as a symbol of cultural identification among young Brazilians, as well as contributing to making the experience more welcoming and accessible. In addition, the game will include a logbook system for recording events, observations and results of experiments conducted during the expedition.

The main benefit of the proposal is to bring scientific knowledge closer to the students' reality through a playful and interactive experience. In this sense, it seeks to stimulate curiosity, logical reasoning, problem-solving, and scientific thinking, as well as broaden understanding of the importance of space research.

Regarding technological development, the languages ​​JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS were used, in addition to tools such as Git and GitHub, intended for source code management and versioning, and artificial intelligence platforms such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, employed as resources to support programming and content creation. Antigravity and Cursor were also used, which assisted in the development of functionalities and the structuring of the game. The integration of these resources enabled the construction of the interfaces, interactive systems, and mechanics necessary for the proposed experience.

The originality of Mars Adventure lies in its integration of space survival, scientific investigation, and challenge-based learning. During development, aspects such as the scientific methodology for data collection in missions, age-appropriate language, information accessibility, challenge progression, and gameplay were also considered, aiming to transform complex scientific concepts into understandable and meaningful activities.

In light of the above, it can be concluded that Mars Adventure presents a proposal for integrating two axes, entertainment and education, using space exploration as a means for constructing scientific knowledge. Its application may contribute to sparking students' interest in science and technology, while simultaneously stimulating skills related to investigation, autonomy, and problem-solving. In this way, the project highlights the potential of digital games as tools to support learning and scientific dissemination.
